timing_policy: These windows are editorial targets, not measured audio durations. An initial normal-rate Aria take measured 21.768 seconds against a 19-second window, so this revision uses a smaller word budget. Generate and measure every current paragraph; fail on an overrun and revise that take. Derive subtitles from actual word boundaries. Never accelerate or invent gameplay to match narration.
recording_policy: Record the actual Main/LifeMode 3D bridge. Camera-only observer tours must carry an INSPECTION label and must not change resident simulation coordinates. Narration describes social attempts without presupposing acceptance. Record save/load results before treating the demonstration as complete.

subtitle_layout.recommendation: Append a 96-pixel matte subtitle band beneath the unchanged 1280x768 game capture. This keeps the existing bottom HUD, menus, needs, and chronicle unobscured.
subtitle_layout.cue_policy: Use measured Edge TTS word boundaries, punctuation-aware breaks, and comfortable reading durations. Prefer 1.1 to 4.5 seconds per cue. Do not infer subtitle timing from these paragraph windows. Verify actual font substitution and the finished image.

segments.title: A town you can enter
segments.text: Welcome to Living Town. This is the running game, connecting the coastal model to the existing life simulation. Forty-nine buildings contain eighty-nine floors, linked by streets, courts, homes, workshops, and a small harbor.
segments.notes: Paused observer opening. Show the actual imported town in Main, not an offline Blender still. Avoid implying every building already has bespoke gameplay.

segments.title: A town you can enter
segments.text: We will play as one resident, then inspect the architecture. Pale walls, dark roofs, stone paving, and planted edges give this town its coastal character. Camera-only inspection will be labelled clearly, separate from the resident's actual movement.
segments.notes: Slow observer camera only; simulation paused. Establish inspection/gameplay distinction before the first transition.

segments.title: Meet Aria and read the HUD
segments.text: We choose Aria through the existing life mode. Her upper-floor rooms sit above the café, with a real route downstairs. The portrait, name, job, money, wishes, and needs belong to the same resident as before. Her identity and rules are retained.
segments.notes: The selector appears at 45 seconds and public start_life('aria') runs at 50 seconds. Begin this paragraph at that genuine selection transition. Owner apartment above café; no direct agent-state edits.

segments.title: Meet Aria and read the HUD
segments.text: The bars track hunger, energy, social contact, fun, and hygiene. Watch them beside the clock. Actions take time. Use the keyboard or a ground click to walk, and E to interact nearby. Zoom changes the view without changing Aria's state.
segments.notes: Keep existing LifeMode HUD readable. Show needs, time, and an available prompt. Camera changes are view-only; no claim that camera motion advances time.

segments.title: Walk the rooms and take the stairs
segments.text: Walls, furnishings, and stair openings define where Aria can stand. The interior grid is finer than the outdoor grid, allowing reachable approaches beside beds and counters. A click through a wall cannot create a shortcut. Movement must find a legal route around it.
segments.notes: Record real input and visible multi-frame walking. Indoor cells are 0.25m; outdoor cells 0.5m. Do not claim continuous physics navigation or a navmesh.

segments.title: Walk the rooms and take the stairs
segments.text: The stair transition has brought Aria downstairs through a legal opening. Private stairs are not available to every resident. At the café table, a meal uses the existing action system. We watch for actual completion and its effect on her needs.
segments.notes: Past-tense recap of the actual stair transition just seen. The full route now shows the table meal; record its actual completion and need effect. Do not infer completion from a preview that skips this dwell.

segments.title: Use a real café fixture
segments.text: We click the visible café counter. The furnishing resolves to an existing functional object and a reachable approach beside it. Its menu offers permitted actions. Aria walks into place and takes time to act. The simulation records the result in her state and history.
segments.notes: Capture actual counter mesh pick, legal menu, walking approach, and completion. Counter aliases can share the physical fixture; do not insist on one alias label if another legal menu resolves.

segments.title: Use a real café fixture
segments.text: The town has seven hundred and fifty-three furnishing assemblies. Only mapped functional objects offer game actions. Decorative shelves and pots do not automatically offer actions. Social attempts retain the existing access checks and the other resident's response. Jobs and wages retain their existing engine rules.
segments.notes: Do not claim all 753 assemblies are interactive. Functional mapping count belongs to the current compiled profile; the compiler may add mapped civic fixtures, so this paragraph deliberately avoids an obsolete total. Social footage must be an actual attempt and acceptance is not guaranteed.

segments.title: Step outside and keep the resident visible
segments.text: Aria leaves through the real café doorway. Her original directional character sheets now appear inside a three-dimensional world. The body keeps normal depth, so roofs and trees can pass in front of it. Ground markers and interaction prompts remain attached to her actual position.
segments.notes: Use genuine exterior portal. Retain buildings and trees. Do not describe sprite art as new 3D character meshes.

segments.title: Step outside and keep the resident visible
segments.text: When geometry blocks the controlled resident, a gold silhouette keeps Aria readable. It appears only during that obstruction. The normal sprite still obeys depth, and the silhouette disappears in clear views. The awning and roof remain in place as we walk toward the plaza.
segments.notes: Show real blocked line of sight under the café awning and a clear view if available. The controlled-only ghost is model-geometry tested at 5 Hz; do not claim all NPCs become visible through buildings.

segments.title: Inspection: rooms and furnishing
segments.text: This is architectural inspection: camera movement, not Aria's travel. The town has five hundred and sixty-one logical zones, including circulation. Two hundred and twenty-three are activity rooms. Halls, landings, and stairs connect those rooms, giving each interior a usable layout. Each group is named and inspectable.
segments.notes: Display INSPECTION — CAMERA ONLY throughout 270–330 seconds. Camera/probe and local cover changes only; preserve resident positions. Counts are final 561 zones / 223 activity rooms, superseding the earlier 549-zone plan.

segments.title: Inspection: rooms and furnishing
segments.text: Look for beds and storage, library shelves and tables, and enclosed bathrooms in hotel suites, with bedroom privacy preserved. Kitchens have sinks, hobs, and distinct refrigerators. Room and floor groups let a cutaway expose one interior while neighboring roofs remain intact. These authored dimensions do not establish building-code approval.
segments.notes: Inspect planned library/home/hotel cameras using actual imported geometry. Some asset detail may be small in the game view; do not replace this with offline stills without labeling them. Widths are nominal authored dimensions.

segments.title: Inspection: streets, elevations, and harbor
segments.text: We remain in inspection mode. Residential rows turn, streets bend, and passages lead into courts. The town has actual surface elevations and gently graded paths rather than a flat board. Roads, plazas, and building pads meet entrance thresholds. The harbor sits at the coastal edge of the same site.
segments.notes: Display INSPECTION — CAMERA ONLY. Show irregular layout and actual surface elevation. No claim of resident traversal along every camera movement.

segments.title: Inspection: streets, elevations, and harbor
segments.text: This is a fictional engineered site, not a surveyed coast or hydraulic study. Terrain heights ground residents, while authored blockers exclude building footprints and water. The movement contract uses the game's spatial grid. Another engine would still need its own decisions about physics, collision, and navigation.
segments.notes: Do not imply certified drainage, shoreline physics, imported GLB collisions, or a generated navmesh. Current bridge movement uses the canonical grid/profile.

segments.title: Inspection: pond and planted routes
segments.text: The park pond cuts into the terrain, with level water above a lower bed and graded banks. A continuous shore, reeds, benches, and a connected loop make the edge readable. This is an authored ornamental pond. Movement rules keep residents on accessible ground beside the water, with planted edges.
segments.notes: Display INSPECTION — CAMERA ONLY. Pond water Z is -0.12 m and bed Z is -0.92 m, with a real basin and banks. Avoid unsupported natural hydrology, swimming, or wildlife claims.

segments.title: Inspection: pond and planted routes
segments.text: Fifty-two planned landscape trees shape streets, courts, and the park. Broad crowns and willows frame the pond. Flower beds, garden islands, low planting, and coastal grasses add smaller detail. Openings preserve doors, paths, and views. The aim is shade and garden enclosure along useful walking routes. Background woodland adds distant enclosure.
segments.notes: The count of 52 refers to planned local landscape trees, not every background forest tree. Show actual connected canopy and horticulture; do not equate projected crown envelopes with measured opaque shade.

segments.title: Return to life and enable autonomy
segments.text: We return to Aria for a social attempt. A visible neighbor must also be reachable. Walls, floors, and access rules matter even when both people appear on screen. Acceptance or refusal belongs to the running game. Read the event and need changes to see the outcome.
segments.notes: End INSPECTION label and restore normal resident view. Actual social attempt is at 450–473 seconds, before autonomy. Do not force another agent's state or promise success. If unavailable, record the real access/availability reason.

segments.title: Return to life and enable autonomy
segments.text: Now we enable autonomy. The existing decision system chooses available actions according to needs, jobs, access, and circumstances. The view follows the movement and activity; it does not create a second simulation. This logic backend runs locally without a downloaded language model or required generated dialogue.
segments.notes: Actual autonomy begins at about 473 seconds, after the social attempt. Enable it through existing LifeMode input/public API. No direct writes to resident position, needs, money, or the clock.

segments.title: Save, continue, and load
segments.text: We save with F five, let the game continue, and load with F eight. Loading rebuilds the view from the saved simulation and resident state. The three-dimensional profile uses a separate quicksave. Incompatible spatial data is rejected instead of loading into a different layout.
segments.notes: Capture real F5/F8 event dispatch and loaded-state evidence. Narration assumes this recorded step succeeds; if it fails, fix/re-record or revise truthfully. Separate user://town3d_quicksave.dat from the legacy save.

segments.title: Save, continue, and load
segments.text: The art remains portable. Blender sources and engine-neutral exports keep named buildings, floors, rooms, materials, and furnishing groups. This bridge binds them to its spatial profile. Frozen file hashes, license credits, and test evidence record the delivered versions, leaving the town usable by other consumers.
segments.notes: Camera can slowly widen while the saved/loaded game remains visible. Engine-agnostic GLB exports are a separate art delivery; avoid implying the runtime loads the high-detail 642 MB GLB. Original maps plus the CC0 HDRI and OFL font are credited in accompanying docs.

segments.title: What the delivery proves
segments.text: The editable runtime passed thirty-six logical checks and twenty-seven visual checks. Legacy regression scenes also passed. The Windows package separately passed normal launch and screen-render checks, rather than the full interaction suite.
segments.notes: Slow whole-town closing view. Distinguish source-runtime gameplay evidence from exported native boot/render proof; do not claim 27 exported interaction checks.

segments.title: What the delivery proves
segments.text: This bridge connects places, retained residents, and observable consequences. It does not establish finished balance or broad hardware performance. The full town loads together. Inspect movement, actions, and saved life.
segments.notes: No LOD, streaming, imported collision authority, or performance guarantee. End on the actual game view, not the concept image. Let the last spoken word finish before 600 seconds.

word_count_method: English word tokens; internal apostrophes and hyphens count as one word.
